feedback: Revise. The candidate is the iteration-5 build (kp 2.5, kd 0.4, ki 0.2, y=0.07, base_speed 1.0) with kd 0.4 changed to 0.35. Iteration 7 raised kp to 3.0 on the same build and reached the best raced score (162.45, vs 160.17 at kp 2.5). Lowering kd to 0.35 on the kp 2.5 build would therefore be a test against a weaker baseline, and the candidate does not carry the best measured kp. Evidence on kd is mixed: kd 0.3 to 0.4 (iteration 3 to 4) raised progress on every track (oval 0.12 to 0.48, s-bend 0.15 to 0.26), but the same change raised oval steering_oscillation from 0.075 to 0.283. A drop to 0.35 may therefore reduce oscillation at some cost in progress. The clean test is to hold the best-raced controller (kp 3.0, ki 0.2) and move only kd, so the race compares directly with iteration 7. Nothing here predicts how the revised design will race. Keep y=0.07 sensors and base_speed 1.0; survival still comes before speed, since no track has more than one finish across 60 trials per race.
requested_changes: Set controller.kp to 3.0 and keep controller.ki at 0.2 (the iteration-7 best raced build, score 162.45), then set controller.kd to 0.35 as the only change from that build. This makes the race a clean kd test against iteration 7.

After the race: if s-bend progress falls below 0.31 or oval progress falls below 0.67 with kd 0.35, return controller.kd to 0.4 and keep kp 3.0. Iteration 4 showed that kd 0.3 to 0.4 raised progress on every track.

After the race: if oval steering_oscillation falls clearly below 0.272 with progress held (at or above the iteration-7 values), keep kd 0.35 and only then test base_speed 1.1. Keep geometry.sensor_positions at y=0.07, because iteration 5 confirmed the forward-sensor lever.
